problems.title: Add two repeating decimals
problems.question: a=0.(199), b=0.(800). Find a+b.
problems.idea: Simplify using the appropriate identity and check the geometry or domain.
formulas: A repeating block of three digits gives the fraction block/999.

problems.title: A square-root inequality
problems.question: Solve √(2x+3)<4.
problems.idea: Simplify using the appropriate identity and check the geometry or domain.
formulas: The radical requires 2x+3≥0; both sides are nonnegative, so squaring preserves order.
steps: The domain is x≥−3/2. Squaring gives 2x+3<16, or x<13/2. Intersect the two conditions.

problems.title: A sum of exact trigonometric values
problems.question: Evaluate tan30°+tan60°+cos45°.
problems.idea: Simplify using the appropriate identity and check the geometry or domain.
steps: The tangent terms sum to 4/√3=4√3/3. Add √2/2.

problems.title: A radical rational expression
problems.question: Simplify $[(\sqrt x+1)/(\sqrt x-1)-4\sqrt x/(x-1)](x+\sqrt x)/(\sqrt x-1)$ and evaluate at x=361.
problems.idea: Simplify using the appropriate identity and check the geometry or domain.
steps: The other factor is t(t+1)/(t−1). Their product is t=√x. At 361 it is 19.
problems.answer: Simplifies to $\sqrt x$ on the original domain; value 19.

problems.title: Distance between centres from a common outer tangent
problems.question: Circle radii are 9 and 4 and their common external tangent segment is 15. Find centre distance.
problems.idea: Simplify using the appropriate identity and check the geometry or domain.
steps: The radii to the tangent are parallel; their difference and tangent segment form perpendicular legs 5 and 15.

problems.title: Irrational inputs with rational means
problems.question: Give two irrational positive numbers with both arithmetic and geometric means rational.
problems.idea: Simplify using the appropriate identity and check the geometry or domain.
steps: Choose a=2+√3 and b=2−√3, both positive irrational numbers.
Their sum is 4 and product 4−3=1, so the means are 2 and 1.

problems.title: Trapezoid diagonals from two base angles
problems.question: A trapezoid has bases 7,15 and angles at the larger base 30°,60°. Find its diagonals.
problems.idea: Simplify using the appropriate identity and check the geometry or domain.
steps: 8=h(√3+1/√3) gives h=2√3. The leg horizontal projections are 6 and 2.
Use lower vertices (0,0),(15,0) and upper vertices (6,2√3),(13,2√3). The diagonal squares are 13²+12=181 and 9²+12=93.

problems.title: Rationalize a denominator containing three terms
problems.question: Rationalize $1/(\sqrt3+\sqrt2+1)$.
problems.idea: Simplify using the appropriate identity and check the geometry or domain.
steps: The first denominator becomes (√3+√2)²−1=4+2√6. Multiplying by √6−2 makes it 4.

problems.title: A product of four distances to an incircle centre
problems.question: An incircle of trapezoid ABCD touches AB at K and CD at P. KA=3,KB=2,PC=1,PD=6. Find IA·IB·IC·ID.
problems.idea: Simplify using the appropriate identity and check the geometry or domain.
formulas: Adjacent base angles supplement each other, giving $r^2=KA\cdot KB=PC\cdot PD$; $IV^2=r^2+t_V^2$.
steps: r²=3×2=1×6=6. The four squared centre distances are 15,10,7,42.

problems.title: A sum of nested radicals is rational
problems.question: Prove that √(11−6√2)+√(6−4√2)+√(9−4√2) is rational.
problems.idea: Simplify using the appropriate identity and check the geometry or domain.
formulas: Recognize each radicand as a square and use √(u²)=|u|.
steps: The radicands are (3−√2)², (2−√2)² and (2√2−1)². All three displayed bases are positive.
The sum is (3−√2)+(2−√2)+(2√2−1)=4, a rational number.
